questions.prompt: What is the capital city of Kosovo?

hints.nudge: A capital city is where a country’s government meets. The other three are capital cities too, of other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Subdivisions” part of the Kosovo article.

questions.prompt: Which of these countries shares a border with Kosovo?

hints.nudge: Two countries are neighbours when you can walk from one into the other. Picture Kosovo on the globe and look at what it touches.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Geography” part of the Kosovo article.

questions.proof: Kosovo shares borders with Serbia to the north and east, North Macedonia to the southeast, Albania to the southwest, and Montenegro to the west.

questions.prompt: Which language is an official language of Kosovo?

hints.nudge: An official language is the one used in schools, courts and government. The other three are spoken in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Modern history” part of the Kosovo article.

questions.proof: However, tensions between the Albanian and Serbian communities led to the Kosovo War.

questions.prompt: What money is used in Kosovo?

hints.nudge: Money names often come from a country’s own words. The other three are spent in other countries.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the opening paragraphs of the Kosovo article.

questions.proof: Kosovo is a partially recognised country located in Southeastern Europe.

questions.prompt: Fill the gap: “These are _____ (which also has limited recognition), and the non-sovereign constituent countries Niue and the Cook Islands.”

hints.nudge: The missing word is a name, not an everyday word. Only one of these names makes the sentence true.
hints.whereToLook: Look in the “Recognition” part of the Kosovo article.

questions.proof: These are Taiwan (which also has limited recognition), and the non-sovereign constituent countries Niue and the Cook Islands.
